description: நாங்கள் அமிர்தா விஸ்வ வித்யாபீடம், நாகர்கோவில் வளாகத்தின் AI & Data Science மாணவர்கள். “Flame in Freefall” சவாலை எடுத்துள்ளோம். நுண்ஈர்ப்பு நிலையில் தீ கோள வடிவில் மெதுவாக பரவுவதால், விண்கலத்தில் அது பெரிய ஆபத்து. NASA-வின் நுண்ஈர்ப்பு எரிதல் சோதனைத் தரவைக் கொண்டு, தீ எப்படி பரவும், எப்போது அணையும் என்பதை கணிக்கும் இயந்திரக் கற்றல் மாதிரியை உருவாக்கி, விண்வெளி வீரர்களுக்கு பயனுள்ள தீ பாதுகாப்பு ஆலோசனைகளை வழங்குவதே எங்கள் இலக்கு.
summary: NASA plans Moon habitats at about 34% oxygen and 8.2 psia, far richer and thinner than ISS air. Fire-Margin is an AI-powered dashboard that ranks, summarizes and interprets NASA's microgravity combustion investigations (PSI) to show how much real evidence exists for fire safety in that atmosphere, and where it is missing. From 274 ISS droplet tests (FLEX), we found that 80% of tests at 25% O2 or higher ended in violent droplet disruption, versus 11% at 21% or lower. In NASA's public PSI data, solid cabin materials stop at 22.2% O2; only three solid samples (Saffire-VI, 2024, not in PSI) have burned near Moon-base conditions. Fire-Margin combines an interactive oxygen-margin map, ML flame predictors with honest uncertainty, a citation-checked AI evidence console, and a ranked list of the experiments NASA should run next.
details:
Live app: https://nasa-space-app-challenge-4gmja93kfafawgepg9uayt.streamlit.app/

Code: https://github.com/antonyjasfer/NASA-SPACE-APP-CHALLENGE

WHAT IT DOES

1) Oxygen-Margin Map: every tested condition from 7 NASA PSI datasets plotted as oxygen vs pressure, with the Moon-base (34% O2 / 0.56 atm) and Artemis (30% / 10.2 psi) targets, partial-gravity equivalents, cool-flame tests and the recommended next experiments.

2) Evidence Console: an AI assistant that answers only from NASA sources, cites every claim, and refuses when the evidence is not there.

3) Flame Predictor: models trained on 274 ISS FLEX tests that predict extinction, disruption or burnout and burning rate, with calibrated uncertainty and an outside-tested-conditions warning.

4) Catalog & Ranking: 24 NASA combustion investigations with a transparent, adjustable relevance score.

5) Saffire-III replay: sensor telemetry from a real fire inside a Cygnus spacecraft.

6) Lessons: Apollo 1, Apollo 13, the Mir fire, and NASA spinoffs on Earth.

KEY FINDINGS

- 24 of 30 FLEX tests at 25% O2 or higher ended in droplet disruption (80%), vs 10.7% at 21% or lower.

- FLEX's lowest pressure was 0.69 atm, above the Moon-base 0.56 atm.

- Solid cabin materials in PSI stop at 22.2% O2; only three Saffire-VI samples burned at 29-31% O2 and ~0.54 atm (verified from NASA ICES-2024 data, not in PSI).

- Gas flames (CFI-G) were tested at 33-39% O2 and 0.50 atm.

- Heuristic (Grashof scaling, clearly labelled): a 1-g ground test at 34% O2 and ~0.22 atm approximates lunar buoyancy.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Python, pandas, scikit-learn, Plotly, Streamlit. Models are validated with GroupKFold by test date, so there is no leakage: extinction ROC-AUC 0.88, balanced accuracy 0.78; burning rate R2 0.71 with conformal intervals at 79.8% coverage. Physics features include the d2-law and the microgravity limiting oxygen index. No synthetic data is presented as NASA data; literature values were checked against the original papers and labelled separately; units were never invented.

IMPACT

A traceable, honest picture of fire-safety evidence for Artemis-era habitats that turns data gaps into a concrete experiment plan for NASA.

USE OF SI

Code and tests were written with Claude Code (Anthropic); research and text with Claude. Investigation insight cards were generated by Claude Code from the NASA Researcher's Guide, with page citations, and are labelled in the app. The in-app assistant uses the Meta API, restricted to retrieved NASA passages. Video narration is AI-generated speech (Microsoft Edge neural text-to-speech). No AI-generated images. All AI-assisted steps are logged in docs/AI_DISCLOSURE.md.
projectRefs: Olson et al. 2019, BASS-II flammability limits
